produced_by: claude-fable-5-1 labellers working in parallel from reference/labelling-brief.txt, each shown the review text alone
notes: Renowned Explorers: International Society. Labelled from snapshot=1788873134, which holds 2,909 reviews: every one Valve reports.

Drawn by `census sample 296970 3551340 548430 275850 1091500 553850 --out data --random 100 --per-category 40 --seed 1 --brief --batch-size 35`. The stratified subset is pooled across all six games, so a category one game barely discusses is supplied by a game that does. The same seed against the same capture draws the same reviews, which is why sample.json need not be kept.

240 labels: 140 stratified and 100 random. The two subsets have different jobs and must not be merged. The stratified labels are TRAINING DATA, so any figure measured over them says what the anchors memorised. The random labels are held back from fitting entirely and are the only ones that measure anything.

Labellers were given the review text and the category sheet, never the classifier's prediction. Agreement measured against this set is therefore not inflated by labellers anchoring on the guess they are being compared against.

66 of the 240 labels (27.5%) are flagged ambiguous because the labeller said the call was genuinely contested. Disagreement on those says as much about the taxonomy as about the classifier, which is why `census evaluate` reports them apart.

This game alone supplies 18 of the 21 categories as a primary label and 21 as a mention. It is the smallest corpus of the six and the only one small enough to crawl in half a minute, which makes it the set to reach for when testing a change end to end.

Measured 2026-09-09 under onnx-community/gte-multilingual-base, anchors pooled from all six sets and fitted for mentions: 53.0% primary agreement on the held-out random subset [43.3, 62.5], macro F1 0.524. Split by how the labeller called it, 52.1% on the 71 clear-cut reviews and 55.2% on the 29 contested ones, the only game of the six where the contested reviews do not score worse. `verdict` reaches F1 0.74, `content` and `language` 0.71, `gameplay` and `genre` 0.66; `story` is the weak row at 0.26, because this game's writing is discussed as part of its expeditions rather than on its own. Every figure in this note names an encoder and a date on purpose: change either and it is no longer about this tool.

Anchors fitted on the other five games and never on this one reach 52.0% against 37.0% for the written descriptions: 26 reviews move to the right category and 11 move away. Fitting on this game's own labels as well adds a single point, to 53.0%, so nearly everything the anchors know about this game came from the other five.

Pooled over all six held-out random subsets, 600 reviews in total, measured 2026-09-09: written descriptions agree with the labels on 37.2%, anchors fitted on the five other games on 51.2%, and anchors fitted on all six on 54.2% [50.2, 58.1], macro F1 0.564. Of the 242 reviews the descriptions and the unseen-game fit place differently, 163 move to the category the labels give and 79 move away (exact McNemar p < 0.0001). Labels from other games are therefore worth about 14 points and labelling the game itself a further 3. Split by how the labeller called it, the pooled figure is 62.1% on the 435 clear-cut reviews and 33.3% on the 165 contested ones. Reproduce with `census fit 296970 3551340 548430 275850 1091500 553850 --out data --leave-one-out`.

The anchors are fitted for mentions rather than for the main subject, which is what `census fit --select` chooses. Fitting for the main subject sets the secondary weight to zero and leaves every category that is usually somebody's second subject with almost no evidence: graphics carried 6 labelled reviews instead of 32 and was found in one review in twenty that raised it. Choosing for mentions costs 1.6 points of primary agreement, which on these 600 reviews is 28 moving one way and 38 the other, p = 0.27.

Because no person has checked these labels, results measured against this set are AGREEMENT WITH A MODEL and must never be reported as accuracy. Two language models agreeing can be wrong together, and the sarcasm and boundary cases where this classifier is weakest are exactly where that correlation is strongest. Set human_verified to true only once a person has labelled a subset independently, and record how large that subset was.

Taxonomy gaps the labellers reported, worth weighing before any future spine: tutorial and onboarding quality, asked for by three separate labellers and currently split between gameplay and difficulty; co-op as a genre trait rather than a multiplayer feature; real-world licensing (teams, players, music) with no home of its own; VR support and immersion; and protests that name a publisher but no requirement, which the offtopic boundary sends to offtopic.
